**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Article XII meets the preferred T4C position:

- **Our convenience right exists** — § 12.2(a)(i) lets Sanofi terminate at will, either in its entirety or on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis, on written notice.
- **No penalty** — § 12.3(c) imposes only wind-down, transition and reversion mechanics; there is no early-termination fee. § 12.3(c)(ii)C actually has RevMed paying *us* post-termination royalties on Termination Products, which is favourable to our side.
- **No counterparty convenience right** — RevMed's termination rights are all cause-based: material breach (12.2(b)), insolvency (12.2(c)), Sanofi Competing Product (12.2(d)) and cessation of development (12.2(e)), each gated by notice, discussion and cure periods.

One open item noted in the rationale rather than flagged: the notice periods in 12.2(a)(i) are redacted (`[***]`), so their length can't be confirmed from this draft — worth confirming against the execution version, recognising that a 30-day notice is atypically short for a collaboration of this kind.
